correctness.rationale: The operator factors through the contractive E_d and is determined by its finite matrix on equal-measure atoms; dyadic automorphisms give identical absolute column sums. Prefix-shell multiplicities 2^(d−ℓ−1), entries 2^(−d)(A_ℓ−b_(ℓ+1)2^ℓ) and the diagonal 2^(−d)A_d give the control objective. The two Bellman branches with k≥2 differ by (1−c)(t−1/2) when the preceding value function is a+c|t−1/2|; the update c↦(1−c)/2 preserves c<1. For one remaining step the value from digit 1 is 1 versus t from digit 0, so 1 is forced for every reachable t<1. If the depth is at least two, the first digit forces t=1/2; only at the second digit and d≥3 does a tie occur. Each subsequent strict action maps an interior state to the opposite open half and cannot hit 1/2, proving alternation and excluding every other candidate. The cases d=1,2 have sole optima (1),(1,1). The update for a recovers the stated (known) sharp value. Xoring the initial frequency segment by N shifts it exactly to the selected blocks, and Walsh multiplication is an L¹ isometry, giving the index classification without changing norms. Summing the digit patterns gives the two listed indices. Replay: repaired RESULT.md, or original lines 24–80; checker.py was inspected, not executed. Finite regression tests are not the all-depth proof.

evidence: For N=Σ b_m2^(m−1), the highest bit of N xor j for j<N is precisely the first bit at which j is smaller. Thus N xor [0,N) is the union of the chosen Walsh blocks. Multiplication by w_N conjugates the Walsh partial-sum projector to P_S, so its norm is L_N.

Dick–Pillichshammer Theorem 2 identifies L_N with the non-normalized binary van der Corput discrepancy d_N, and p. 4 states the same sharp formula on the dyadic block. value.rationale: The binary dyadic filtration and Walsh Lebesgue constants are standard exact endpoint objects. Knowing one high-norm selector and the sharp value does not say whether many distinct scale patterns tie, or which alterations are possible. The all-depth necessity-and-sufficiency theorem answers that structural question: one binary tie, forced alternation among subsequent nonterminal choices, and a forced terminal digit. Through the isometry it also gives a complete optimizing-index classification for the discrepancy/Walsh formulation. This distinct equality question, not the recomputation of the known maximum, justifies retention.
